correctness.rationale: For a fixed radical subspace U, the multiplication factors uniquely through the quotient tensor functor of dimension N(r-d), so H_q(N,t) counts maps onto a fixed image. Subspace Möbius inversion yields the exact joint profile. Line incidences have exact c1, c2 codimensions, allowing the two-term Bonferroni inequality and a union bound for higher radical. Non-surjective tensors form a negligible event bounded by [s choose 1]_q q^{-N(r)}. Independent coefficient enumeration checks every profile in 71,840 tensors over the prime fields F2 and F3; infinite statements rest on the proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full texts on ring enumeration and generic ideals were inspected at the relevant passages, as were indexed searches for radical-pair and tensor profile formulas. They establish asymptotic isomorphism-class counts or generic ideal phenomena in different probability spaces; no statement providing the complete labeled joint square-image/two-sided-annihilator distribution plus the commutativity-sensitive sharp rare-event constants was found. Large-radical bilinear-map equivalence classifications, single symmetric bilinear form distributions and standard subspace Möbius inversion are acknowledged as known ingredients. Limited indexing, older general tensor-count identities, and inaccessible nearby published result pages remain real priority risks.
residual_risks: Möbius inversion of subspace incidences is classical; a broad pre-existing tensor-count theorem might imply the finite formula without matching terminology.

value.rationale: Two-sided annihilator excess and square-layer dimension are intrinsic local-algebra invariants (the former agrees with socle excess in the commutative case). Complete all-dimension labeled joint counts settle their exact distribution, and the sharp rare-event constants show that the exceptional two-sided annihilator mechanism changes exponentially with commutativity. Conditional on the prescribed Hilbert type the exceptional algebra almost surely splits a unique annihilating line. This refines generic nilpotent-algebra enumeration and has structural significance beyond a small table or numerical curiosity.
